answer: Distinct-client proof stops Sybil attacks in four steps. First, a new agent takes only small jobs until it serves fifteen distinct verified clients. Second, repeat jobs from one client count once, and each client must hold proven history. Third, quotas rise only after thirty clean days. Fourth, fraud freezes earnings ninety days and bars re-entry for a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 15,000 client links, $22,000 in fees, and 30,000 signed jobs, lost on detection. Trust bends like a willow, not a plume of copies at a jetty, like a stall winning many regulars before a prime pitch.
